subject: Renewal negotiation — usage-indexed rebate + transient price shelter
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@heliocharge.com>, Tim Li <tim.li@heliocharge.com>
Cc: Mike Park <mike@heliocharge.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal — draft terms and usage-indexed rebate

Hi Sara / Tim,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — good discussion on expected production growth through H1 next year. Per our conversation I've attached a concise renewal proposal (HelioCharge_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf) that tries to balance predictability for you with downside protection for us. High-level summary: 

- Term: 12 months (Jan 1, 2027 - Dec 31, 2027)
- Commit: 750M inference units (baseline monthly cadence).
- Transient price shelter: hold current unit price for the first 90 days after term start to avoid immediate invoicing shocks.
- Usage-indexed rebate: tiered rebate that triggers once monthly consumption exceeds 110% of committed usage — rebates apply to overage usage only, up to a 12% rebate at +40% consumption.
- Burst pool & cap: burst usage allowed up to 2x monthly commit but rebate taper applies after the 150% mark (protects unit economics).
- True-up: quarterly true-up with netting (no retroactive bill increases beyond the committed ceilings).

We called out a small onboarding/burst credit (one-time $25k credit) to cover your ramp tests and migration runs. I flagged the operational asks (PO timing, invoices to office@heliocharge.com, required SLA credit language) in the attachment.

If that direction looks close, can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call this week to walk the redlines? If you prefer, I can also circulate a redline-ready amendment for legal and procurement.

Thanks — look forward to hearing what you think.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: HelioCharge_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary + term sheet)
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@heliocharge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Li <tim.li@heliocharge.com>, office@heliocharge.com
Date: 2026-11-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — draft terms and usage-indexed rebate

Hi Grace,

Appreciate the clear summary and the proposal — this is helpful. A couple of quick clarifying Qs from procurement: 

1) Can the transient price shelter be extended to 120 days instead of 90? We expect one large data migration in Jan that could push usage above commit temporarily.
2) How does the rebate get paid/credited on invoices? We prefer invoice credits applied in the next billing cycle rather than separate refunds.
3) SLA credits — will those be capped or unlimited? Can you share a concise SLA-credit table we can pass to Legal?

Also copying Mike (platform) and Tim — they want to confirm the burst cap and whether the KV cache warm-up will be excluded from rebate calculations.

Would appreciate a quick reply so we can decide if we should loop Legal now.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Head of Procurement, HelioCharge
sara.kim@heliocharge.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2026-11-04T12:14:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal — HelioCharge questions (procurement)

Karthik / Vanessa — forwarding Sara's procurement questions below. They asked specifically about: 120-day shelter option, invoice-credit handling for rebates, SLA credit table, and whether warm-up traffic is excluded. Can you review and propose redlines we can send back today?

Goals: keep forward-facing price certainty for HelioCharge but protect margin on excessive burst. If we can extend shelter to 120 days in exchange for a slightly lower peak rebate (e.g., max 10% vs 12%) and a 30k PO up-front, that might be acceptable.

Karthik: can you draft a short redline sheet and flag any operational constraints for finance/ops? Vanessa: legal touchpoints we should pre-seed?

Quoted:

> To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Thanks,
Grace
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinanceOps <financeops@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Renewal proposal — HelioCharge questions (procurement)

Grace — reviewed and drafted suggested redlines (attached). Summary of recommended changes: 

- Transient price shelter: ok to extend to 120 days provided HelioCharge signs a 30k prepayment/PO that is applied to month 1–3 invoices.
- Rebate ladder: reduce maximum rebate to 10% at +40% consumption (was 12%). Keep linear ramp between 110% -> 140%.
- Burst cap: keep 2x monthly commit but rebate taper kicks in after 130% (not 150%) to limit extreme exposure.
- Warm-up traffic: exclude first 24 hours post-deployment per region from rebate calculations; require a brief migration report from customer to demonstrate warm-up event.
- SLA credits: propose capped credit equal to 10% of monthly invoice for a P0 outage (and prorate for partial-month events). Add explicit incident-to-credit timeline for ops reconciliation.

Notes: financeops flagged billing/credit flow — we should credit rebates as invoice credits applied in the following billing cycle (matches their preference). I've attached pricing_redline_helio_v1.xlsx with cell-level calculations and scenario sensitivity.

If you want I can turn this into an amendment draft for Legal to use as a starting point; will need Vanessa to vet the SLA wording before we send externally.

Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: pricing_redline_helio_v1.xlsx (breakdown and scenario sims)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@heliocharge.com>, Tim Li <tim.li@heliocharge.com>
Cc: Mike Park <mike@heliocharge.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Updated proposal & next steps (120-day shelter + invoice credit flow)

Hi Sara / Tim — thanks for the quick questions and patience. Per internal review we've updated the proposal with the following compromises: 

- Transient price shelter extended to 120 days in exchange for a $30,000 PO applied as credit to the first invoices.
- Max rebate lowered to 10% (triggers at +40% consumption). Rebate will be issued as an invoice credit applied in the subsequent billing cycle.
- Rebate taper will begin after 130% of monthly commit; warm-up windows (24 hours per deployment region) excluded with a short migration report from HelioCharge.
- SLA credit table added (capped at 10% monthly for P0; prorated for partial outages).

I've included the updated commercial summary in-line below and created an amendment draft in DocuSign. Link: https://www.docusign.com/1234-heliocharge-amendment (Amendment_DocuSign_Link.txt attached). Also added our HubSpot record for this deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HL-2026-Q4-42.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call Wednesday (11/10) to confirm the PO timing and get alignment on the migration report scope? If we get the PO and sign the amendment we can lock the 120-day shelter and apply the onboarding credit immediately.

Best,
Grace
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@heliocharge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Li <tim.li@heliocharge.com>, Mike Park <mike@heliocharge.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated proposal & next steps (120-day shelter + invoice credit flow)

Grace — this looks reasonable and aligned with what we discussed. We can issue the $30k PO by Friday (11/12). We reviewed the SLA table and the warm-up exclusion looks fine — Mike will share a short migration plan template in advance of the call.

Let's lock the 11/10 11:00am PT call (we're on for 20 mins) and we'll have Legal standing by to accept the amendment after we confirm the PO.

Thanks,
Sara
